title: Ines and the Drop
premise: Tamsin Kavanagh, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent a decade laundering her own past into an unremarkable life, receives a debt notice for a favor she never performed—signed with her mother's maiden name. The 'Drop' is an old network of fixers and money-movers that trained her as a child before she burned her identity to escape it, and its dying founder has named her heir. Hunted by the network's enforcers, a rival syndicate, and her own agency's internal affairs unit, Tamsin must decide whether inheritance means obedience or destruction. In the end she dismantles the Drop from inside, sacrificing her clean name and her career, but walks out owning the one thing the network never gave her: a self she chose.
about_author: M. M. Okonkwo is a former compliance analyst who spent eight years tracing shell companies across three continents before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people trapped inside systems they helped build.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Tamsin Kavanagh's POV. A routine day at the Financial Conduct Authority: flagging laundered funds that all look legitimate because she knows exactly how legitimacy is faked. The emotional beat is quiet dread—she's good at her job because she was trained by criminals, and someone at work is starting to notice patterns in her own accounts.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A courier delivers a sealed envelope: a debt instrument for one favor, rendered with interest, signed 'Adeyemi'—her mother's buried maiden name. She traces the courier to a shuttered dry cleaner she recognizes from childhood. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of a carefully built life.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, intercut with a cold open from enforcer Viktor Rehn. The debt's terms surface: report to the Drop's custodian within seven days or her fabricated identity gets sold to the highest bidder—including her employer. Beat: claustrophobia; every exit she maps is already watched.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in young Tamsin's voice. How the Drop found an orphaned girl in Lagos, taught her ledgers, languages, and lies, and how she fled at nineteen by faking her death. Beat: tenderness curdling into betrayal—the network was family until it was a cage.

chapters.title: Internal Affairs
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Tamsin and IA officer Dana Whitlock. Whitlock opens a file on Kavanagh's impossible travel history while Tamsin pre-emptively requests leave. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; two investigators circling the same woman.

chapters.title: The Dry Cleaner
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She breaks into the old front business and finds the Drop's dead-drop still warm—recent cash, recent instructions—and a photograph of herself taken yesterday. Beat: fear sharpening into fury; they never lost her, they were waiting.

chapters.title: Custodian
chapters.summary: Tamsin meets Odile Ferran, the Drop's aging custodian, in a Lisbon chapel. Odile reveals the founder, 'the Tailor,' is dying and has named Tamsin sole heir to the network's books. Beat: seduction of belonging—the offer is genuinely tempting.

chapters.title: The Books
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Shown a fragment of the Ledger: forty years of payments reaching into banks, police forces, and one entry referencing her own escape, paid for by someone inside the network. Beat: vertigo—her freedom was purchased, not won.

chapters.title: Whitlock Closes In
chapters.summary: Dana Whitlock's POV. Whitlock finds the fake death certificate from 2014 and realizes Kavanagh is a ghost with a badge. She sits on it, unsure whether she's hunting a criminal or being played by one. Beat: moral ambiguity deepens on both sides.

chapters.title: Viktor's Lesson
chapters.summary: Viktor Rehn's POV. The enforcer tests Tamsin by staging a mugging; she disables him with techniques only the Drop teaches. He reports: the heir remembers everything. Beat: grudging respect between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: The Rival
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A second bidder emerges: the Meridian syndicate offers to buy her debt and erase her—if she delivers the Ledger first. Now three factions want her, and the deadline halves. Beat: pressure cooker; trust becomes a currency she can't mint.

chapters.title: Mother's Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin travels to Lagos and finds her aunt, who reveals the Tailor was her mother's brother—and that her mother didn't die; she ran, and the Drop caught up with her. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance; the debt is generational.

chapters.title: Double Entry
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She agrees to inherit, playing loyal, and begins copying the Ledger via memorized fragments—her old training turned against her trainers. Beat: cold exhilaration; the student out-techniquing the school.

chapters.title: The Tailor
chapters.summary: First meeting with the dying founder, told through Tamsin's POV. He doesn't want an heir; he wants absolution, and confesses he ordered her mother's death when she tried to leave. Beat: horror and pity entangled; the monster is frail and sincere.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Whitlock's POV colliding with Tamsin's. Meridian leaks Tamsin's real identity to IA to force her hand; Whitlock confronts her in a parking garage and chooses, provisionally, to listen instead of arrest. Beat: an unlikely alliance struck over shared contempt for corrupt systems.

chapters.title: The Vault Night
chapters.summary: Tamsin, Whitlock, and a coerced Viktor execute the plan: drain the Ledger to a secure server during the quarterly vault audit. Everything goes wrong when Odile anticipated the betrayal. Beat: betrayal met with betrayal; the plan half-succeeds at terrible cost—Whitlock takes a bullet.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, hospital corridor. With Whitlock critical, Tamsin weighs releasing the Ledger publicly, which destroys innocent lives tangled in it alongside the guilty. Beat: the theme made explicit—the price of survival is paid in other people's blood too.

chapters.title: Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Tamsin accepts the inheritance fully, taking command of the Drop's remaining assets to control the burn from inside. Odile submits; Viktor defects to her side. Beat: dark coronation; power fits her hand too well.

chapters.title: Meridian Falls
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She feeds Meridian a poisoned version of the Ledger, letting the syndicate's own buyers destroy it, then hands the evidence trail to Whitlock's IA team. Beat: ruthless satisfaction shadowed by self-recognition—she's using their methods perfectly.

chapters.title: The Last Audit
chapters.summary: Climax. Confrontation with the Tailor, who triggers a dead-man's switch to release her identity unless she inherits publicly. Tamsin lets it fire—choosing exposure over ownership—and watches the network's clients scatter as the full Ledger hits every regulator at once. Beat: catharsis through surrender.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: Falling action, Tamsin's POV. Arrested, debriefed, and quietly released as a cooperating witness, she resigns from the agency. Whitlock, recovering, burns the last copy of her file—an act of mercy neither names. Beat: exhaustion and grace; survival redefined.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Epilogue in Tamsin's POV, now living under no name at all, teaching bookkeeping at a community center under the childhood name her mother gave her: Ines. A stranger leaves an envelope on her desk; she reads it, smiles, and shreds it unread. Final beat: the debt cycle ends where she decides it ends.
